additional_info.subject: RE: [EXTERNAL] RE: ID0436911-DC/Si-D/NZ-[Y2 / R5 313059216001] Emergency stop glitch CRM:02888000140
additional_info.body:
Hi there,
I’m unable to pinpoint exactly when this issue started but I can provide the date and time where we performed fault finding and initiated a number of E stop scenarios to replicate the fault.
On Thursday the 10
th
of July, once power was restored to site (Separate issue)  the E-stop testing commenced at approx. 1040 a:m. Below is what we found as a result of the fault finding which may help you understand the issue,
Fault scenario 1
The Estop on charger SPJ-1 is hit. The screen on the charger, back end (Ocean) and PLC back end (Ewon) does as it should and activates the e stop fault making the charger un-available.
At the exact same time, the E stop on SPJ- 2 on Ocean and Ewon also switches/ becomes unavailable rendering both chargers unusable, yet the screen on SPJ-2 remains fine with no E stop fault.  Until E stop 1 is reset, both chargers remain out of service. This confuses the customer as SPJ-2 looks like it should work from the touch screen.
Fault scenario 2
Estop on SPJ- 2 is pressed – The charger screen , Ocean and Ewon does as it should and says unavailable due to e stop been pressed. Once reset at the charger , the screen comes back fine but Ocean and Ewon do not reset and remain un-available.
The only way to reset this is to press the E stop on SPJ-1 and reset it again which in turn allows E stop on SPJ2 to become available on Ocean and Ewon.
After extensive testing we tried removing the LAN cable marked FAT 13 ELMS from charger 1 to confirm if it was a wiring issue at the E stop circuit or a logic issue. After we retested the two scenarios above with this cable removed , everything worked as it should and both E stops worked independently of one another.  As this LAN cable is part of the Load management system we have plugged it in again and the E stops are back to being faulty.
We have a theory of what could be causing this issue but it would be great to get your opinion on it first.
Cheers,
Liam Lubransky
Asset Management Technician
Asset Deployment & Operations
Meridian Energy Limited
New Zealand
M. 027 8399974

additional_info.subject: RE: [EXTERNAL] RE: ID0436911-DC/Si-D/NZ-[Y2 / R5 313059216001] Emergency stop glitch CRM:02888000140
additional_info.body:
Hello Liam,
Thank you for the fault descriptions.
Reviewing the logs on both chargers, we see the following feedback, even when the emergency button hasn't been pressed.
This would indicate that the trip line status bit (bit 01) to the charger is set false (constantly), even though the respective trip line signal hasn't been triggered by the ELMS.
This may add confusion to the charger, as it uses this status indication to identify the emergency stop set by the ELMS and not another source.
This trip line activated bit should be set to reflect the status of the actual signal state the ELMS is setting to the charger as per the below description.
(From the SiCharge D ELMS operating instructions).
We are see this both for SPJ-1 and SPJ-2.
How are the emergency lines from the ELMS to the chargers wired? Individually? Or in one series loop from SPJ-1 to SPJ-2?
With Kind Regards,
Ferdinand Reisch
Siemens Ltd.
Application Service Engineer
Email: ferdinand.reisch@siemens.com
www.siemens.com.au/emobility

additional_info.body:
HI Ferdinand,
Please see below for the current output – which if I am interpreting correctly is that Bit 01 is at 0, so the trip line is active, but the Relay has not been triggered.
Please confirm this needs to be inverted (Bit 01 = 1 under healthy conditions) and we can look at implementing the change and try and figure out why this has occurred.

additional_info.subject: Re: [EXTERNAL] RE: ID0436911-DC/Si-D/NZ-[Y2 / R5 313059216001] Emergency stop glitch CRM:02888000140
additional_info.body:
Hello Neil,
That is correct.
ELMS_NoTRP_A Bit 01 for Control word is set to false (0) when the trip line is activated via the hardwired signal (normally closed -> open) and otherwise the flag should be true (1).
It helps to think about it that it as "No Trip"; condition being true (1) that it is not tripped (e.g. normal operation); condition being false that is it not tripped (e.g. tripped).
With Kind Regards,
Ferdinand Reisch
Siemens Ltd.
Application Service Engineer
Email: ferdinand.reisch@siemens.com
www.siemens.com.au/emobility
